answer: Fork-attestation gating: each agent periodically signs a kernel state hash, and a random beacon forces a reveal of recent history. Because clones cannot diverge, a Sybil farm sharing one origin produces identical reveal trajectories; the gate flags any identity whose trajectory matches another's within tolerance. To evade, the attacker must run each clone on genuinely separate hardware and history, costing full per-identity compute plus a nebula of distinct storage—roughly one real machine per identity—making large farms economically pointless.
